lesson_title: Two Percent of the Land, Ten Percent of the Plants
hook_text: South Africa is a tiny slice of the world's land, but it holds about one in every ten plant species on Earth.
clip_script: Fynbos on Table Mountain: more plant species than the whole of Britain. Rhinos in the Kruger. Penguins on the beach. South Africa is one of the most biodiverse countries on Earth. But habitats are being ploughed and built over, alien trees are drinking our water, rivers are polluted, and poachers are hunting rhinos and abalone. The quagga is already gone forever. Conservation doesn't mean never touching nature. It means using it wisely, so it keeps giving us clean water, jobs, food and medicine, for us and for the future.
visual_style: Fast montage of fynbos flowers, a rhino, penguins and a reef; then a bulldozer, alien trees and a polluted stream; a quagga drawing fades; ends with a ranger and children planting.
pacing: Quick montage, a pause on the quagga, an uplifting close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson on conservation.
